messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: Dedicated pool pressure detected for tenant=sinOSYS-prod (vpc-78). GPU queue depth spiking, 95th latency > 5s. Severity: P1. @amanda-sre auto-page

amanda-sre: seeing it. DC us-west-2 dedicated pool is at 98% GPU util, queueing on nvidia0..nvidia3. Errors: `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and request timeouts.

ben-oncall: joining. Can we confirm this is tenant-local or cluster-wide?

amanda-sre: it's tenant-local. Pool size 12 GPUs reserved for sinOSYS-prod. Requests/sec doubled after a customer rollout at 09:22 UTC.

carla-cs: sinOSYS reported degraded latency and a few 5xxs to their L3 earlier. They're on a support call now asking for ETA.

suresh-eng: quick check: logs show long KV cache miss storms and several long-running heavy generation jobs (seq_len ~2048, top_k sampling) from a small set of API keys.

devops-jen: trying `rdwctl pool describe sinOSYS-prod` -> shows no burst enabled. Config: "burst_policy": "disabled", "autoscale": "reserved-only".

amanda-sre: options: 1) enable burst to shared capacity (fast restore but may impact best-effort customers), 2) evict the longest-running jobs for the tenant (risk of user-facing errors), 3) request manual burst from capacity team (takes ~10-20m). Thoughts?

ben-oncall: what's SLO / contract? Do they have burst in their contract?

carla-cs: per contract, sinOSYS has the option for paid burst but not auto-burst. They've been on a Dedicated Reserved plan; sales would need to approve if we bill. They asked for emergency access once.

amanda-sre: given impact (P1, customer on call), propose temporary emergency burst for 30m to clear queue, then revert. We'll log as chargeable and notify sales & legal. Need a +1 from ops.

devops-jen: I can flip burst on now: `rdwctl pool update sinOSYS-prod --burst=enabled --burst-cap=4` and route to shared pool. This will open 4 GPUs from shared.

ops-bot: Running: rdwctl pool update sinOSYS-prod --burst=enabled --burst-cap=4 (initiated by devops-jen). ETA for allocation: ~90s.

amanda-sre: do it. Also prepare eviction plan if burst doesn't keep up: identify top 3 longest-running request IDs and cancel. Use `rdwctl requests list --pool sinOSYS-prod --sort=duration`

devops-jen: burst applied. Shared GPUs allocated. Metrics: GPU util dropping from 98% -> 72% in 2min, queue depth halved.

carla-cs: informing sinOSYS on the call: "We've temporarily enabled emergency burst to restore service; this is chargeable per contract. We'll follow up with billing and a post-incident RCA."

amanda-sre: monitoring. If we see repeat in 30m, we'll escalate to capacity team for quota increase or ask customer to throttle long-running seq jobs.

suresh-eng: I also pushed a temporary rate-shape to block requests with seq_len>1024 for their API keys so we avoid repeat heavy runs while they investigate. Command: `rdwctl keys update --key K-XXXX --max_seq_len 1024`

ben-oncall: handoff: I'm on the sinOSYS bridge until 1720000200, then amanda takes over. Leaving notes in pagerduty.

amanda-sre: acknowledged. Current status: service degrading -> restored by burst. Next actions: follow-up RCA, billing notification, policy review for auto-burst guardrails.

carla-cs: I'll send customer post-incident note and schedule a follow-up with product for long-job guidance.

ops-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-3319. Assigned: amanda-sre.

amanda-sre: closing the on-call page for now but keeping ticket open. Final note: emergency burst allowed recovery without evictions. We'll prepare a targeted mitigation (quota change + prompt guidelines) to avoid churn. :thumbsup:
